trickyParts: The warning and the arm share one payload write. rememberWait replaces readyMerge's rememberArm: both wait paths go through it, it writes the payload at most once per run, and the merge-waiting notice is enqueued inside that same pgx.BeginFunc under the row's lease, so a row can never be recorded as warned without its notice nor the reverse. A reopen's requeue of the same issue and head clears the payload, so the replacement writes nothing and the notice rolls back with it.

A cause permanentRefusal reports never warns: that row ends and finishRefused already tells the architect (merge-refused, merge-stalled, merge-removed). Without that guard the architect would get two notices for one ending row.

The hour runs from outbox.created_at, the queue at READY's acceptance, because nothing in the daemon records when GitHub was first asked; created_at survives every retry, the arm-remembering write and a reopen's upsert.

READY's conflict refusal kept its place in the order but lost its old reason (it was refused before the checks were read so a missing check would not be reported as the cause); the reason that survives is that GitHub computes no merge ref for a conflicting head, runs no pull_request workflow on it and will not merge it.

gh api graphql --paginate follows a query only when it declares $endCursor and selects pageInfo{hasNextPage endCursor}; the same query without them returns one page and looks complete. The one shape is written verbatim into both documents that carry it.
deviations: The plan's task A said to remove the stand-in's checkRuns/statuses fields once no test sets them. The workflowRuns field, the actions/runs route and the base repository id are gone.

TestHandoffCompleteReadyOnARepositoryWhosePlanHasNoRulesets became TestHandoffCompleteReadyRefusesTheSameWhateverTheBaseRequires: rather than keeping only the surviving assertions, it inverts the old test's subject - a base requiring a check, a base requiring none and a rulesets read that would answer 500 all give the same three outcomes - which also proves READY makes no rulesets read at all.
